spec.purpose: Use released cub commands and one WorkshopResult record for the same three jobs shown on the website.

objectIdentity.rule: The file hash identifies exact bytes. The object-set hash identifies the accepted Kubernetes objects across file names and document order.

jobs.question: I need a configuration. How should I run this?
jobs.result: Select an exact source and starting configuration before changing it.

jobs.question: I have a configuration. Is it right?
jobs.result: Keep exact objects, findings, omitted checks, and source context in workshop-result.json.

jobs.question: I have an accepted configuration. Can I promote it?
jobs.result: Retain the accepted object-set hash in ConfigHub, then preview the linked downstream promotion.

examples.label: Helm values written with AI

select.note: Read the maintained package choices without downloading or installing the package.

materialize.command: cub helm template nginx nginx --repo https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami --version 24.0.2 --namespace nginx --values examples/byo-helm-values/reviewed-values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered
materialize.note: Helm turns the pinned chart and values into Kubernetes objects.

record.command: node scripts/create-config-workshop-result.mjs --candidate ./rendered --cub-check cub-check.json --source-type helm --source bitnami/nginx --source-version 24.0.2 --source-record config-catalog/config-workshop-command-contract/helm-source-and-intent.yaml --configuration-decision config-catalog/review-decisions/byo-nginx-ai-values-24-0-2-reviewed.yaml --output workshop-result.json

retain.dryRun: cub variant upload --dry-run --component byo-nginx-ai-values --variant reviewed --space byo-nginx-ai-values-24-0-2-reviewed --granularity minimal --annotation workshop.confighub.com/object-set-sha256=sha256:502d8c85470455fa4152f8d0abb9d1582552e830148e90335e9649cbfd42f397 ./rendered
retain.execute: cub variant upload --component byo-nginx-ai-values --variant reviewed --space byo-nginx-ai-values-24-0-2-reviewed --granularity minimal --annotation workshop.confighub.com/object-set-sha256=sha256:502d8c85470455fa4152f8d0abb9d1582552e830148e90335e9649cbfd42f397 ./rendered
retain.bindAcceptedIdentity: cub unit update byo-nginx-ai-values --space byo-nginx-ai-values-24-0-2-reviewed --annotation workshop.confighub.com/object-set-sha256=sha256:502d8c85470455fa4152f8d0abb9d1582552e830148e90335e9649cbfd42f397 --change-desc "Bind the accepted object set"

vary.command: cub variant create staging byo-nginx-ai-values-24-0-2-reviewed --space-pattern template:byo-nginx-ai-values-24-0-2-staging --environment Staging --unit-annotation workshop.confighub.com/object-set-sha256=sha256:502d8c85470455fa4152f8d0abb9d1582552e830148e90335e9649cbfd42f397

release.note: Publish only after the destination Space has a release target and its required checks and approvals pass.

examples.currentLimit: The retained base carries the canonical object-set annotation. Each derived variant still needs its own identity because a namespace or field change produces a different object set.

examples.label: Existing Kubernetes YAML

select.note: The supplied directory is already the selected source.

materialize.note: The source already contains Kubernetes objects, so checking can start without rendering.

record.command: node scripts/create-config-workshop-result.mjs --candidate examples/plain-yaml/acme-web --cub-check cub-check.json --source-type kubernetes-yaml --source examples/plain-yaml/acme-web --source-version source-r001 --source-record data/base-variant-records/records/kubernetes-yaml-acme-web-base.yaml --output workshop-result.json

retain.dryRun: cub variant upload --dry-run --component acme-web --variant base --space plain-yaml-acme-web-base --granularity minimal --annotation workshop.confighub.com/object-set-sha256=sha256:4c7fac59248636842c560c5fcb2076bf9ffe2ed2e4576ff754b51c8dc21fed6c examples/plain-yaml/acme-web
retain.execute: cub variant upload --component acme-web --variant base --space plain-yaml-acme-web-base --granularity minimal --annotation workshop.confighub.com/object-set-sha256=sha256:4c7fac59248636842c560c5fcb2076bf9ffe2ed2e4576ff754b51c8dc21fed6c examples/plain-yaml/acme-web
retain.bindAcceptedIdentity: cub unit update acme-web --space plain-yaml-acme-web-base --annotation workshop.confighub.com/object-set-sha256=sha256:4c7fac59248636842c560c5fcb2076bf9ffe2ed2e4576ff754b51c8dc21fed6c --change-desc "Bind the accepted object set"

vary.command: cub variant create staging plain-yaml-acme-web-base --space-pattern template:plain-yaml-acme-web-staging --environment Staging --unit-annotation workshop.confighub.com/object-set-sha256=sha256:4c7fac59248636842c560c5fcb2076bf9ffe2ed2e4576ff754b51c8dc21fed6c

release.note: Publish only after the destination Space has a release target and its required checks and approvals pass.

examples.currentLimit: Checking and ConfigHub retention are proved. A linked staging promotion and delivery have not run for this example.

boundaries: cub check is local advisory evidence. ConfigHub validation remains a separate managed control.
A promotion command is a preview until destination checks and the promotion itself have run.
Helm materialization does real work. Literal Kubernetes YAML is already materialized, so that stage is recorded as a no-op.
The public OCI digest, exact file hash, canonical object-set hash, and ConfigHub data hash have different roles.
